title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization Alone can Improve Adversarial Robustness
main_claims: SAM alone improves adversarial robustness significantly over standard training without sacrificing clean accuracy, an unexpected benefit beyond SAM's intended sharpness reduction.

SAM and adversarial training (AT) share a common mechanism: both eliminate non-robust features by adding perturbations, but SAM applies implicit moderate perturbations in feature space while AT applies explicit strong perturbations in input space.
SAM can serve as a lightweight substitute for AT under requirements of no accuracy loss and no significant computational overhead.
methodology: Empirical experiments train PreActResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 for 100 epochs with SGD, SAM (ρ∈{0.1,0.2,0.4}), and AT (various ℓ∞ and ℓ2 bounds). Robustness is evaluated with 10-step PGD attacks. Theoretical analysis uses a binary classification model with robust and non-robust features (following Tsipras et al.) to prove that SAM increases the weight on robust feature x1 beyond standard training.
key_results: On CIFAR-100, SAM (ρ=0.4) achieves 78.7% natural accuracy and 28.3% ℓ∞-robust accuracy (ε=1/255), vs. 76.9% and 13.6% for standard training.
On CIFAR-10, SAM (ρ=0.4) achieves 94.7% natural accuracy and 56.1% ℓ∞-robust accuracy (ε=1/255), vs. 94.6% and 39.6% for standard training.
AT achieves higher adversarial robustness but consistently lower natural accuracy than SAM across all perturbation bounds.
limitations: Robustness evaluation uses only PGD attacks; adaptive attacks or certified robustness are not assessed.
The theoretical analysis is limited to a simplified linear binary classification model and may not generalize to deep nonlinear networks.
The paper is a workshop submission and has not undergone full peer review.
relevance_to_rq: Peripherally relevant: shows that SAM's effects extend beyond sharpness reduction to include feature-space robustness properties, which partially aligns with the RQ's hypothesis that representation-level effects (not just sharpness) explain SAM's OOD gains. However, adversarial robustness differs from CIFAR-C corruption robustness.

key_quotes.text: SAM applies small perturbations implicitly to the feature space to maintain good natural accuracy performance, while AT utilizes direct data augmentation magnitudes
key_quotes.context: Mechanistic comparison of SAM and AT in terms of perturbation space and strength

key_quotes.text: we find that using only SAM can achieve superior adversarial robustness without sacrificing clean accuracy compared to standard training, which is an unexpected benefit
key_quotes.context: Main empirical finding of the paper

key_quotes.text: both SAM and AT improve robustness of the trained model by biasing more weight on robust features
key_quotes.context: Theoretical unification of SAM and AT mechanisms
